newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares at record high, Electrolux surges.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares at record high, Electrolux surges.

text.p: Swedish shares closed at record high levels on Thursday, lifted by gains for telecoms group Ericsson and cheered by a rally in household appliance group Electrolux.
The Stockholm bourse's general index rose 0.26 percent to a closing record high of 2,897.31 in turnover of 6.67 billion crowns.
Dealers expected a strong market also on Friday.
"If the U.S. remains at these levels, prices could rise," a trader said. "We also saw a strong interest rate fall in the afternoon which the market didn't have time to fully react to."
Electrolux skyrocketed 64 crowns to 529 after announcing a 2.5 billion crown restructuring programme. Dealers were divided on whether the share could keep rising or if the surge was an overreaction.
Ericsson rose seven crowns to 298.5 after rising 5.5 crowns a day earlier on reports that Merrill Lynch had upgraded its profit forecasts for the group.

Drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn dropped 7.5 crowns to 264.5, stung by rumours saying it would post a second quarter profit of 43 cents a share, below market expectations of 50 cents. The group said it had no plans to issue a profit warning.
Rival Astra ended flat at 126.5 after dipping in intra-day trade on news about a German court ruling against its German Losec patent. Astra said it would appeal the ruling.

Investment and medical technology group Incentive jumped 25 crowns to 732 after selling half its stake in ABB AB for 12.4 billion crowns as part of an ongoing divestment to focus on medical technology.

Investment company Investor bought 6.5 billion crowns worth of shares in ABB AB and dropped 5.5 crowns to 392 on disappointment that it bought the stake instead of focusing on new growth sectors as promised.
ABB AB fell 3.5 crowns to 111. This is the same price that Morgan Stanley Dean Witter will offer to sell the shares it bought from Incentive to institutional investors.
